A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QHFlow study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Hamiltonian-prediction experiments on MD17 and QH9, SCF acceleration measurements, and appendix ablations and error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds architectural-control results in Appendix F.4 and Table 11.

M1.justification: The architecture, flow-matching procedure, sampling algorithms, and implemented fine-tuning objective remain substantially unchanged. However, v2 replaces LogNormal with Normal for the TE radial prior in Sections 4.2 and C.3 while retaining LogNormal in B.1 and C.4. This contradiction prevents determining whether the prior actually changed or the revision introduced a textual error.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four MD17 molecules, four QH9 splits, and SCF-initialization task. The new architectural controls use the existing QH9-stable (id) setting. Revised sample counts do not establish additional task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 11 adds evaluated QHFLOW (Regression) and QHFLOW (W/o S embed) comparisons against the full model and QHNet*. Comparator membership in the existing MD17, QH9, prior, fine-tuning, and SCF comparisons is retained.

E3.justification: Table 6 revises QH9-dynamic from 269,800 structures and 2,698 molecules to 299,800 and 2,998, with corresponding split-count changes. Table 7 changes the reported QH9 learning rate from 1e-3 to 5e-4. Table 11 introduces regression and overlap-removal controls. These are reported-setting revisions, not evidence of reruns; Appendix E.1 still states 2,698 molecules.

E4.justification: New Appendix F.4 and Table 11 test the contributions of flow matching versus regression and of the overlap-matrix embedding. Existing prior-choice, fine-tuning, predictive-variance, error-distribution, and molecule-size analyses remain. The additional SCF figure redisplays existing measurements rather than introducing another robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions describe five inference repetitions that vary the initial-noise seed and report means and standard deviations in Tables 4 and 10. Existing uncertainty values and distribution summaries are retained; no new repeated-run count, confidence interval, or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 11 newly reports Hamiltonian MAEs of 35.85 for regression and 25.24 without overlap embedding, versus the retained full-model result of 22.95 microhartree on QH9-stable (id), alongside orbital metrics. Existing benchmark tables and Figure 3 retain their scores. The MD17 summary changes from 71% to 73% error reduction without corresponding Table 1 score changes.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendix A.1 replace the incorrect sum-of-orbitals wavefunction with a noninteracting KS construction and a Slater determinant, adding density relations. Section 4.1 revises the approximate-energy definition to match the retained Appendix B.2 objective. Core equivariance theorem statements remain. The new density integral in v2 Equation (16), however, contains |Psi| rather than |Psi| squared.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the claimed MD17 error reduction from 71% to 73% and explicitly identifies the previous best model as the comparison target. The main claims about generative Hamiltonian prediction, invariant priors, energy-alignment fine-tuning, and SCF acceleration retain their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix F.4 adds interpretations attributing accuracy gains to flow matching and overlap information. The revised limitations acknowledge the missing theoretical connection between Hamiltonian error and SCF acceleration and suggest one-step models to reduce inference overhead. The earlier 10–20% training-overhead estimate is removed; most applicability restrictions are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link on the first page and discloses PySCF B3LYP/RKS settings for the existing SCF experiment: integration grid level 3, at most 50 cycles, and otherwise default parameters. Reported hyperparameters and sample counts are revised. Hardware, software-version information, and day-based training-time estimates largely remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kornilov et al.'s Optimal Flow Matching as a possible future approach to reducing inference overhead. The introduction and related work slightly shift the contrast with regression toward structural correlations and predictive uncertainty. The remaining cited works are retained after renumbering.

P1.justification: The revision rewrites and expands the KS-DFT explanation, clarifies SCF percentage reporting, moves and revises limitations from Appendix F.4 to the main text, and reorganizes Appendix F around added subsections. Affiliations and publication-header text also change. Most of the original narrative and section structure remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 11 and a redisplay of SCF results with inference-time zoom insets in Figure 5. Figure 3 is restyled and receives an expanded caption. Appendix tables and figures are regrouped; the earlier Figures 5–8 remain as Figures 6–9 rather than being replaced by new analyses.

improvement.justification: Table 11 supplies useful controls for the existing design, while the repository link and explicit SCF settings improve reproducibility documentation. Clearer SCF reporting and the corrected Slater-determinant description also help. These constitute a limited net gain, tempered by newly conflicting Normal/LogNormal specifications, the missing square in Appendix A.1 Equation (16), and unresolved sample-count inconsistencies.
